'Federico, how's this one?'
'Extrapolating based on the Sanctilaminium Ambrosii outer wall searchlight covers, it has not been used in at least a year.'
'It looks a little worn, but the size is about right. We'll just have to cut it open down the middle, wipe it clean, then we can place that flower inside.'
'Have you obtained the inhabitants' permission?'
'Oren dragged a batch of supplies over when he sent the commandos, and these are the scraps the inhabitants don't need anymore. Leave it to me once we're on overtime—I don't want to see you cracking it open by hand.'
'We have at most an hour before the monastery resumes its journey.'
'We'll make it. That reminds me, though, Federico...'
'What is it?'
'I don't believe that gardener left a will.'
'Monastery resident Clément Dubois has received an appropriate burial. He did not leave behind an executable will, nor any other personal estate.'
'Um, you know I'm trying to ask, right?'
'You wish to understand why I am preserving this flower.'
'This isn't your first time handling an assignment with so much baggage, right? But I've never seen you leave a keepsake for yourself before... Are you doing okay?'
'My assignment is complete. But there are still unaddressed doubts raised by the Sanctilaminium Ambrosii.'
'If I'm remembering correctly, there was this quote from some Saint: 'A gun needs a target, but not every question can have an answer.''
'I cannot overlook any issues. They will directly impact any followup assignments.'
'*sigh* What am I even worrying over? Wait, don't tell me you questioned His Holiness when you went to report the mission progress?'
'I did, but did not receive an answer.'
'So that's why you're insisting on giving a nearly burnt-out flower another drying. Now I get it. Still, I have to say one thing—whether you can keep it preserved or not doesn't depend much on this glass bell I'm cutting. It's already dead. It's not the flower it was before, Federico.'
'Richele, your word count in this conversation is significantly above-average.'
'Ahaha, just making small talk. And I'm not even going to ask where you got that average from. Alright, it's settled—after we give this a wash, we'll stick it onto the pedestal. It'll be as pretty as what they sell in stores.'
'Thank you.' Federico takes the grimy glass bell from his coworker's hands, and walks out of the junk-filled shed.
'Well, then. What kind of answer will you find, Laterano's newest Saint?'
uniequip_003_excu2:
Statement on complaints regarding mission LNH****0142

I was assigned to mission LNH****0142 five days ago, as part of maintaining public order for the 100-day celebration of Adytum Reliquiarum. A stall owner requested a substitute after suffering accidental burns, and the case was referred to me by the organizing committee.
The items sold by the stall were handicrafts. The owner was in a depressed mood when I completed the mission and returned the stall to him. He asked if none of the visitors understood his art. I responded that I was unable to answer the question as I did not have any interaction with the visitors. The citizen became angry and asked whether I was the reason that none of the handicrafts were sold. I did not understand the question but deemed it necessary to placate the citizen, and therefore offered to purchase one of the handicrafts. He calmed down and complimented my taste in art, then asked which one I liked, as well as my thoughts on the handicrafts sold by the stall. My answer was as follows:
The stall sold models of the Reliquiae in various sizes, a common subject in today's Laterano. For instance, the Curia's new almond cookies are in the same shape. Upon closer inspection, it can be seen that the models are not precisely to scale, the details inexact, and the craftsmanship flawed. I was not particularly fond of the handicrafts, and my offer to purchase was due to other reasons.
The citizen interrupted me before I finished. He loudly declared his intention to file a complaint before leaving.
Other executors at the scene witnessed what occurred that day. I am filing this supplement to the unfinished statement at the recommendation of one of them:
I was not particularly fond of the handicrafts, but I offered to purchase one because the doodles on one of the models caught my attention. The Reliquiae models sold by the stall had different doodles; this particular one had blue clouds drawn on it. It reminded me of drawing lessons from my childhood, when many children my age used blue crayons to draw clouds on white paper, even though clouds are not blue. I asked the teacher about this, who said I was right, but did not correct the others. This confused me, but many things in life are confusing, the quantity of which has only increased with age. I had almost forgotten about the question until I was reminded of it by the model. I spent some time looking at it, then at the Reliquiae itself, before realizing that I now understood how clouds could be blue.
I had not visited the Adytum Reliquiarum until the celebrations. The last time I saw It, It was glowing bright red as it computed an answer, until Andoain Agathangelos and I put an end to it. Now, people scribble their wishes and other things upon it, and depictions of it can be found in the form of crude handicrafts, almond cookies, balloons, mittens, and mouthwash bottles. It did not provide an answer, and we will continue to have more questions, endless questions, just as I experienced in the course of growing up. As such, I wished to purchase the model as a reminder not to be shackled by questions, for the answer will eventually come someday.
Finally, I have requested a box of Reliquiae almond cookies to placate the citizen in question. I will deliver it to the citizen's residence once the request is approved.
